headline: Insurers stop issuing subordinated bonds due to soundness burden
summary: Ahead of next year's basic capital soundness regulation, insurers have effectively halted subordinated bond issuance. Nine insurers had a basic capital K-ICS ratio below 50% as of end-June, per NICE Investors Service.
why: Subordinated bonds are a capital instrument insurers use to meet solvency requirements, so halting issuance affects their funding options before new rules take effect.
